title: Maximum Number of People That Can Be Caught in Tag
summary: In a game of tag, where players are divided into 'it' and not 'it', you are given an array indicating 'it' and 'not it' players, and a distance.
statement: In a game of tag, where players are divided into 'it' and not 'it', you are given an array indicating 'it' and 'not it' players, and a distance. 'It' players can catch any 'not it' player within a certain distance. Determine the maximum number of 'not it' players that can be caught by 'it' players.
constraints: team has 1 through 100000 entries: zero denotes an agent and one denotes a person.
Each agent catches at most one person within index distance dist, and each person can be caught once.
Return the maximum number of catches.
hints: After sorting positions, matching the earliest feasible pair leaves the most room for everything later.
Use one pointer for agents and one for people; match when close enough, otherwise discard whichever position is too far left.
If |a-p|<=dist advance both and count; else advance the smaller position.
An unmatched earlier position cannot reach any later opposite position when it already lies too far left, while exchanging a crossing match for the earliest pair never hurts feasibility.
editorial: An unmatched earlier position cannot reach any later opposite position when it already lies too far left, while exchanging a crossing match for the earliest pair never hurts feasibility.

tests.explanation: The first two agents can match the two people, so two are caught.
No agent shares an index with a person, so distance zero permits no catches.
